objective: DIRECTIONAL-RIGIDITY-20261023-001 proved that 18 of the 30 three-place tiling contacts are rigid in direction (free stripes or straight walls) and certified the other 12, whose coin-pinned walls can turn at both ends of the diagonal edge, as selective; for the four whose walls have no choices it proved that an odd class contradicts exactly when every periodic wall collides with its own copy on that cylinder, and that the condition is sufficient for all twelve. Prove the converse for the eight whose walls have choices, describe the direction structure it implies, and decide whether every contact whose walls can turn is selective on every large enough torus.
status: Complete 2026-10-24: walls with choices. For every three-place tiling contact with a constant frame, a direction has an assignment exactly when a periodic wall crosses its cylinder without meeting its own copies (necessity through cyclic covers); directed walls keep the first quadrant together. Simple cycles of the wall graph do not suffice for the four honeycomb contacts with a free place (111, 125, 159, 215), whose good walls must sometimes repeat a state. Planted staircases make the other eight bending contacts selective on every torus with sides at least 3; the four stay open. Recommendation: Continue with the cost of reading a direction (2/3), deferred to the owner.
title: Walls with choices: when contacts select directions
